text.text_excerpt: The second we stepped in here, I said to myself "I like this place!". Black Penny is definitely a local spot, just a bit off Bourbon but far enough away that locals and the people who are done partying by 11PM pop in just to have a drink or two. The bartender Gio is great and remembered us from the night before. Their beer list is downright impressive. The beer menu alone is nearly 3 pages. There is something for everyone, including your regular beers such as Heinekin and Stella. But if you come here, I encourage you to try a craft beer. It's well-worth it. Everyone here is so friendly and welcoming. Even if you're "new" to the 'hood, they still make you feel like you belong and will add ...

I really like this place. It's dark, old, creepy-ish but not filled with tourists (mostly). It's on the edge of the quarter so it's not too hard to get to (well, the Hard Rock Hotel mess does make it a little difficult). Large beer list was pretty dope, and the bartender was knowledgeable and super friendly. He even gave us some kumquats for hanging out. It does smell damp but that's because ya the Quarter, the building is old, and New Orleans is a swamp. My only complaint is that on a Friday night, the bathrooms get SO SO SO gross. Just bring some travel size hand sanitizer, ladies, and you'll be fine. One of the better bars in the French Quarter.

I see that this spot is listed as a "dive" bar, but with the atmosphere and an amazing beer list, I think this watering hole ranks a few notches above that. Yes, this bar is so much more than a dive bar. It's a treasure on North Rampart. Granted, this bar isn't located in the best area, but bring a buddy and you should be fine. We stopped in here after a show at the Saenger. I had been wanting to try this place ever since some beer loving friends mentioned that Black Penny has a legit beer selection. I liked this bar as soon as I walked in- it was nice and dark with a seating area off to the side, if you didn't want to sit at the bar itself. We decided to sit at the bar and I was thrilled...
